assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Line 79 asserts status == 200: reinstating the regression (the attach back inside the handler's error path) makes the read answer 500, so it reddens — shown in repro-before-fix.log and negative-control.log. Line 82 asserts body['schedule'] is None and line 83 that CREW_FAILURE, the message the test's own _crew_rows stub raises, appears in body['schedule_error']: the message crosses the code under test's exception catch and its f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}" formatting, and on the reverted path schedule_error is absent entirely, so the assertion raises KeyError rather than holding — it is not a comparison of a value against the same variable the test passed in. Line 84 asserts exactly one serve-logger record carrying the helper's marker, so a helper that logged zero or several times reddens.

After the crew-row failure the first read must carry schedule None; then _crew_rows is replaced with a stub returning [] and the second read must carry a non-null schedule with schedule_error absent. A helper that degraded permanently — caching the failure or nulling the schedule on later reads — reddens the second half, so the assertion is independent of the first read's outcome.

route_results._served_result is made to raise, and the read must still answer 500 with body['error'] == 'distributed_project_state_invalid'. Widening the new helper's catch to cover the stored-result read (or wrapping that read in the same degradation) makes the status 200 and reddens both assertions, so this case guards the catch's blast radius rather than echoing it.

findings.text: follow-on: the recorded ruff command chains `ruff check ... && ruff format --check ...`, and ruff check exits non-zero on the repository's pre-existing backlog, so the format check never ran and the log shows only check's output. Its last line reads 'Found 17 errors.', while the manifest's evidence_inputs states 'ruff on reckon/serve.py: 19 findings at base and 19 after (no addition)' — a figure no log on disk supports, so the no-addition claim rests on an unrecorded comparison. I re-ran both read-only on the two changed paths: ruff check reports 'Found 17 errors.' (all inside reckon/serve.py; the new test file is clean) and ruff format --check reports '2 files already formatted', exit 0. The done-when's format clause therefore holds, but the record does not show it, and the two counts disagree.

follow-on: the population log's header names the base revision — '# revision: 54c22f415ec859a1b557fa15805dde8f83f7a6ec (dirty: serve.py + new test)' — not the head 1a0d696f6a54ca1a701c42e631f0819b4804d933 whose code it measured; gate-head.log:1 carries the same header. The run is sound (the change was present in the tree, and head.log:2 does name 1a0d696f), but a reader comparing these headers against the manifest's head claim sees a contradiction and cannot tell from the log alone which revision the 65-test population measured.

item_verdicts.call_sites: Production runtime code that can reach the change: reckon/serve.py:3332, the /_discover/<project> branch of Handler do_GET, is the sole caller of _attach_schedule_for_read; reckon/serve.py:1792 is the helper's own delegation to _attach_schedule, whose only other callers are tests. _attach_schedule drives schedule_report over the stored inventory and _crew_rows(mounts, project), so a failure listing the live crew rows is the reachable failure the goal names. The node's own test files are excluded.
item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit against the base: a single commit, 1a0d696f, touching three files. reckon/serve.py adds the 31-line _attach_schedule_for_read helper between _attach_schedule and _docs_relative, and changes the one line in the /_discover/ handler from _attach_schedule to _attach_schedule_for_read; the helper delegates to _attach_schedule so the existing signature and behaviour are unchanged on the success path. tests/test_a_schedule_failure_leaves_discovery_served.py is a new three-case file reusing the served fixture from tests/test_the_slow_routes_answer_from_stored_results.py. The fragment records the before/after measure. Nothing else changed.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when names tests/test_a_schedule_failure_leaves_discovery_served.py. The manifest records head.log (3 passed, EXIT=0), negative-control.log (2 failed 1 passed, EXIT=1), repro-before-fix.log (2 failed 1 passed, EXIT=1) and population-head.log (65 passed, EXIT=0), and I read each: the three cases cover a crew-row failure answering 200 with a null schedule and a schedule_error, exactly one serve-logger line, a restored listing carrying the schedule again, and a stored-result read failure still answering 500 with distributed_project_state_invalid. The done_when's clause that every importer of reckon/serve.py shows no added failure is a focused 65-test population here and is delegated to the coordinator's merge run by the done-when itself; its ruff clause is met but not shown by its own log (see finding).
item_verdicts.goal: The goal is to serve discovery with a null schedule and a named schedule error when attaching the schedule fails. reckon/serve.py:1777-1804 adds _attach_schedule_for_read, which wraps _attach_schedule in a try, and on failure returns a copy of the payload with schedule set to None and schedule_error set to the exception's type and message, logging the failure once; reckon/serve.py:3332 is the only production caller and passes the result straight to _send_json, so the read answers 200 with the stored inventory intact. The helper is wired in exactly where the goal names.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read; status complete, one commit 1a0d696f, the landing line written in place of a plan edit, the gate command recorded literally, and five logs named. Its baseline_suite and after_suite keys are empty, so I derived the delta from the gate logs the manifest does name: no failing id appears in the node's own arms (head.log 3 passed EXIT=0, population-head.log 65 passed EXIT=0); module-window.log fails only on reckon/budget.py, reckon/crew/review.py and reckon/ledger.py, all pre-existing and outside the node's write scope, and it does not name reckon/serve.py. added_failure_count is therefore 0. Its stated ruff figure does not match the log it cites (see finding).
item_verdicts.write_paths: The source prompt fences reckon/serve.py, tests/test_a_schedule_failure_leaves_discovery_served.py, docs/evidence/fragments/the-site-answers-fast-and-agrees/a-schedule-failure-leaves-discovery-served.html and an unused docs/figures/ tree. git diff --stat 54c22f41..1a0d696f names exactly the first three: serve.py +31/-1, the new test file +117, and the fragment +14. No path outside the declared scope was touched and no plan file was edited.
